briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The past 24 hours saw a significant escalation of covert and overt military activities. A Wall Street Journal report revealed a clandestine Israeli military base in Iraq used for strikes against Iran, leading to an Israeli attack on Iraqi forces who nearly discovered it. Concurrently, Hezbollah launched multiple explosive drones and rockets into northern Israel, injuring three reservists, while Israel conducted extensive retaliatory strikes on over 85 Hezbollah targets in Lebanon, including a strategic underground facility in the Beqaa Valley.

IRAN
Military operations against Iran included what Press TV describes as a "US-Israeli war of aggression," citing a strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab that allegedly killed 26 female teachers and 120 students. Controlled explosions of unexploded munitions were reported in Bandar Abbas. Iranian Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref claimed that US-Israeli strategy to weaken Iran's core industries through bombing petrochemical and steel plants failed.
Internally, Mojtaba Khamenei is reportedly heavily involved in decision-making, operates in hiding, uses human messengers, and is recovering from various injuries (burns, knee, back, ear) sustained in a bombing of Ali Khamenei's residence. The nationwide internet shutdown entered its 11th week, causing a reported $335 million direct loss to the ICT sector and an estimated 55 trillion Toman (approximately $1.3 billion USD) in digital economy losses, forcing many online vendors to street vending. There were reports of unrest in Piyan village, Izeh, with 7 arrests and 3 injuries. The judiciary has frozen assets of 264 government opponents.
Economically, an oil slick observed near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export terminal, was interpreted by Western experts as a sign of infrastructure collapse and potential oil dumping due to full storage, though Iranian officials denied this, attributing it to a European tanker.
Regarding leadership decisions, Iran's Foreign Minister emphasized that halting aggression and abandoning unreasonable demands are necessary for diplomacy. Iran is reportedly delaying its official response to US peace proposals. Iran also set strict conditions for its participation in the 2026 World Cup, including visa issuance, respect for the national team/flag/anthem, and increased security.
Air defense performance details were not available, but Iranian officials asserted responses to all US provocative acts in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's National Security Committee Chairman, Ebrahim Azizi, warned Bahrain against supporting US-backed anti-Iran resolutions, stating, "Do not risk closing the Strait of Hormuz on yourselves forever." Iran also threatened to cut global internet cables under the Strait of Hormuz.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included the interception of multiple hostile aerial targets and rockets from Lebanon, with alarms activated across the Western Galilee in communities like Hanita, Shlomi, Ya'ara, Metzuba, Betzet, Rosh HaNikra, Milouot North, Liman, Hof Achziv, and Baram. A rocket impact was identified in an open area near Baram. IDF forces operating in southern Lebanon also intercepted several rockets. A Wall Street Journal report indicated Israel established a clandestine military outpost in Iraq's western desert to support its air campaign against Iran, and subsequently attacked Iraqi troops who nearly discovered the base.
Casualties reported include three IDF reservists wounded by Hezbollah explosive drones near the Lebanon border—one seriously and two moderately—with an unmanned engineering vehicle also sustaining damage. Two individuals were reported injured in Shlomi by an explosive drone.
The home front air defense systems were actively engaged, successfully intercepting several suspicious aerial targets. Sirens were triggered widely across northern communities.
Politically, Gadi Eisenkot of the Yesh Atid party called for Prime Minister Netanyahu to resign, holding him responsible for October 7th and subsequent events. Netanyahu reportedly warned the US against prolonged negotiations with Iran and stated that any agreement not fully dismantling Iran's nuclear program would be unacceptable.
Civilian impact included frequent warnings and alarms in northern communities. Police used water cannons against demonstrators in Paris Square, Jerusalem, leading to two arrests. Investigations are underway into the fatal shooting of a Rahat resident by Border Police.
Strategically, Israel reportedly communicated to the US that a resumption of war should include the destruction of Iran's energy infrastructure, which it believes can be achieved within 24 hours.
Economically, S&P affirmed Israel's 'A' credit rating with a stable outlook, citing economic resilience but warned of potential negative action if regional tensions escalate. Wizz Air canceled flights to Israel until May 26.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Ground operations in the Gaza Strip included the IDF and Shin Bet destroying a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) weapon manufacturing and storage site in the northern Gaza Strip, which was also utilized by Hamas.
Casualties and humanitarian situation reports indicate Press TV claiming a "quiet genocide" in Gaza and showing aftermath footage of Israeli bombardment of residential buildings in Al-Shati' refugee camp. A Palestinian delegation warned the EU about threats to the Christian community in Gaza due to Israeli policies. Israel is preparing to release and deport two Sumud Flotilla activists after over a week in detention.
No specific updates on Gaza ceasefire negotiations were provided.
In the West Bank, Israeli settlers launched raids, burning homes and cars and attacking a Palestinian child. Israeli forces compelled a Palestinian family in the northern West Bank to exhume their son’s grave and move the body.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included launching multiple explosive drones and rockets into northern Israel. One such drone seriously injured an IDF reservist and moderately injured two others near the border, while another damaged an unmanned engineering vehicle. Hezbollah claimed targeting Israeli Merkava tanks in Al-Bayadah and Nimr al-Jamal sites with drones, and launching drone swarms and rocket barrages at settlements. Hezbollah claimed 26 military operations, including rocket strikes on a base near Haifa.
Israeli strikes saw the IDF hitting over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, drone launching sites, rocket launchers, and buildings. An underground weapon manufacturing site in the Beqaa Valley was also targeted. Israel also struck two primed rocket launchers and targeted Hezbollah operatives. Press TV reported Israeli airstrikes killed 11 civilians in Al-Saksakieh and 20 civilians in other southern Lebanon areas, and hit a civilian vehicle in Al-Saadeyet and a highway south of Beirut, describing these strikes as defying the ceasefire agreement.
No specific UNIFIL incidents or displacement reports were provided.
Cross-border exchanges were frequent, with multiple alerts and interceptions on the Israeli side, met with extensive Israeli retaliatory strikes in Lebanon. The US State Department announced talks between Israel and Lebanon on May 14-15 to discuss a peace framework.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Militia activity reports indicate an Iraqi government committee, including current and incoming Prime Ministers, is reportedly close to completing a plan to disarm pro-Iranian militias, which is intended for presentation to the Trump administration. Iraqi Border Guard forces seized an air balloon carrying 34kg of Captagon from Syria. Explosions were reported in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah in northern Iraq, resulting from drone attacks on Kurdish Iranian opposition party headquarters.
Airstrikes and proxy operations include a Wall Street Journal report of a clandestine Israeli military outpost in Iraq's western desert supporting its air campaign against Iran, which led to an Israeli attack on Iraqi forces who nearly exposed it. There were reports of dozens of Iraqi oil tankers damaged in a crash in Bisngul, Syria, injuring three Iraqi drivers and killing one civilian driver.
Spillover effects included US MQ9 and AH-64 Apache helicopters being spotted over Baghdad, and a USAF Bombardier E-11A flying over Iraq. The Russian embassy in Baghdad posted a #Russia_Iraq_cannot_separate message for Victory Day.
Diplomatically, Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam met with Syria's HTS-led regime leader Abu Mohammed Al-Jolani in Damascus.

GULF STATES
Regarding military posture, Bahrain announced the arrest of 41 individuals allegedly linked to Iran's IRGC, a move fully supported by Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry. The Bahraini army declared readiness for the third time. Gulf States reportedly spent an additional $17 billion on 4200 Patriot missiles, indicating preparations for war.
Diplomatically, the US and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) are pushing a UN Security Council resolution regarding the Strait of Hormuz, with Chapter VII (military action) removed, and a focus on dialogue, but still calling for Iran to stop attacks, clear mines, and halt transit fees. Russia stated it will object to this resolution.
Economically, the Strait of Hormuz reportedly experienced "relative calm," with the US awaiting Iran's response to peace proposals. However, MarineTraffic data claimed no commercial ships passed through the Strait in the last 24 hours. A Qatari LNG carrier successfully navigated an Iran-approved northern route in the Strait for the first time since the war began. Bloomberg reported global energy reserves are rapidly declining due to the Iran war disrupting Persian Gulf oil flow, increasing the risk of price spikes and shortages. An analyst suggested the UAE is concerned about the end of the Iran-US war, anticipating new dynamics with Iran.
US pressure on the Strait of Hormuz continues, with CENTCOM claiming its maritime blockade against Iran is fully effective, diverting 58 commercial vessels and disabling 4.
The UK announced it is sending HMS Dragon, a Type 45 destroyer, to the Middle East to be ready for a potential international mission to protect shipping in the Strait of Hormuz once conditions allow.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Clandestine Israeli Base in Iraq:** A Wall Street Journal report indicated Israel established a secret military outpost in Iraq's western desert to support its air campaign against Iran, leading to an Israeli attack on Iraqi forces who nearly discovered the site.
2.  **Escalated Hezbollah Attacks:** Hezbollah launched multiple explosive drones into northern Israel, injuring one IDF reservist seriously and two moderately, and damaging an unmanned engineering vehicle. This is part of a broader escalation where Hezbollah claims 26 military operations and rocket strikes on a base near Haifa.
3.  **Extensive Israeli Retaliation in Lebanon:** The IDF conducted extensive strikes, hitting over 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon, including weapon depots, drone launch sites, and an underground weapon manufacturing facility in the Beqaa Valley.
4.  **Bahraini Arrests and Regional Stance:** Bahrain arrested 41 individuals allegedly linked to Iran's IRGC, with Saudi Arabia explicitly supporting these actions. Iran's National Security Committee Chairman, Ebrahim Azizi, warned Bahrain against supporting US-backed resolutions on the Strait of Hormuz.
5.  **Strait of Hormuz Dynamics:** A Qatari LNG carrier successfully navigated an Iran-approved northern route through the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first such passage since the war. Simultaneously, MarineTraffic data suggested no commercial ships passed through the Strait in the last 24 hours. The US and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) are pushing a UN Security Council resolution for the Strait, though with military action clauses removed. The UK is deploying HMS Dragon to the region for a potential international mission to secure the Strait.
6.  **Iran's Energy Infrastructure as a Target:** Israel reportedly communicated to the US that any resumption of war against Iran should include the destruction of Iran's energy infrastructure, which it believes can be achieved within 24 hours.
7.  **US Sanctions on China:** The US imposed new sanctions on ten individuals and companies, many based in China and Hong Kong, for allegedly aiding Iran's defense sector, specifically for Shahed drones and ballistic missile programs.
8.  **Iran's Caspian Sea Route:** Reports indicate the Caspian Sea has become a critical trade route for Iran to bypass the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, with Russia supplying drone components through this route.
9.  **Civilian Casualties in Lebanon/Iran:** Press TV reported an Israeli airstrike killed 11 civilians, including a child and her mother, in Al-Saksakieh, southern Lebanon. Separately, Press TV alleged a US-Israeli strike on Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Minab, Iran, killed 26 female teachers and 120 students.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high, evidenced by Hezbollah's increased use of explosive drones and Israel's extensive retaliatory strikes in Lebanon, including strategic targets. Israel's stated objective to target Iran's energy infrastructure if war resumes, coupled with Iran's threats to cut internet cables under Hormuz and escalate military confrontations, points to a high risk of broader conflict. Active flashpoints remain the Israel-Lebanon border and the Strait of Hormuz, with covert Israeli operations in Iraq adding another dimension. Military posture changes include the deployment of a UK destroyer to the Middle East and substantial Patriot missile investments by Gulf States. Iran's declared red lines involve any confrontation with its vessels in the Gulf and any attempt to restrict its access to the Strait of Hormuz. Israel's red lines include continued Hezbollah aggression and Iran's nuclear program. The US has signaled a potential "Freedom Plus" operation if diplomatic efforts fail.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is characterized by a diplomatic push with Iran, offering sanctions relief, while maintaining a hawkish stance on Iran's nuclear program and threatening "Operation Freedom Plus" if negotiations fail. CENTCOM insists its maritime blockade is effective. The US also imposed new sanctions on Chinese and Hong Kong firms for aiding Iran's defense sector.
Gulf States, including Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, are taking a firm stance against Iran-linked activities, with Bahrain arresting 41 individuals and Saudi Arabia supporting these actions. They are also heavily investing in air defense and are co-sponsoring a UN Security Council resolution on the Strait of Hormuz.
EU members, including France and Germany, have called for regional de-escalation. The UK is deploying HMS Dragon to the Middle East for a potential international mission to safeguard shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Russia is actively supporting Iran, facilitating trade via the Caspian Sea route and supplying drone components. Russia also stated it would object to the US/GCC-drafted UN resolution on the Strait of Hormuz.
Turkey's President Erdogan stated opposition to the expansion of the US war against Iran. Costa Rica is upgrading its diplomatic representation in Jerusalem, and the US State Department announced Israel-Lebanon talks for a peace framework.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions exist regarding the status of the Strait of Hormuz, with some sources reporting "relative calm" while others claim "not a single commercial ship has passed" in the last 24 hours. There are also conflicting reports on the Kharg Island oil slick, with Iranian officials denying it resulted from infrastructure collapse and attributing it to a European tanker. Reports on Mojtaba Khamenei's injuries show minor discrepancies in detail. Unverified claims include an Israeli espionage scandal involving soldiers, uncorroborated explosions in Tehran and Bandar Abbas (though controlled explosions were later reported in Bandar Abbas), and claims of Iranian tanker seizures. Propaganda indicators are evident in Press TV's and Omid Dana's strong anti-US/anti-Israel rhetoric and pro-Iran narratives. Reporting gaps include specific casualty numbers for various incidents, detailed updates on Iran's nuclear program, specific details of the alleged Israeli secret base in Iraq, and comprehensive updates on the humanitarian situation in Gaza.
